title: 🚨 An Indian vessel has reportedly sunk in the Red Sea. Thankfully, all 13 India
description:
🚨 An Indian vessel has reportedly sunk in the Red Sea. Thankfully, all 13 Indian sailors were rescued. But the bigger question remains: Who was behind the attack?

On 4 August 2026, the Indian vessel MSV Faize Noore Oliya reportedly sank near Yemen after being struck by what is believed to have been a rocket or drone.

According to available reports, the Yemeni Coast Guard successfully rescued all 13 Indian crew members.

However, responsibility for the attack remains officially unconfirmed.
The Yemeni government has accused the Iran-backed Houthi movement, while India's Ministry of External Affairs has described the incident as "deeply concerning" but has not attributed the attack to any specific group.

This incident comes at a time when global shipping routes are already under pressure due to tensions in the Middle East. With disruptions around the Strait of Hormuz, many commercial vessels have increasingly relied on the Red Sea corridor one of the world's most strategically important maritime routes.

If the attack is eventually confirmed to have targeted an Indian vessel, despite India having no direct conflict with the Houthis, it could have significant implications for regional maritime security and India's commercial interests.

As investigations continue, the focus remains on establishing the facts and ensuring the safety of international shipping.

title: #NEETEXAM
description:
#NEETEXAM

NEET UG-2024 results were declared recently and a record number of 67 students secured AIR 1 with a percentile score of 99.997129. 
But the results have raised eyebrows at the National Testing Agency (NTA) as students demand re-exam citing paper leaks, unfair grace marks, and irregularities.

Here’s what happened…

👉  Right after the results were declared, questions were asked on how such an unprecedented number (67) of students secured 720/720 and AIR 1. The number in 2023 was just 2, with students belonging from Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh. 

👉  Another issue raised was that some students have reportedly scored 718, 719. Achieving these scores seemed mathematically impossible. 

However, here’s what the NTA said… 👇

"NTA received few representations and Court cases from the candidates of NEET (UG) 2024 raising concerns of loss of time during the conduct of the examination on 05.05.2024. 
Such cases/representations were considered by NTA and the normalisation formula, which has been devised and adopted by the Hon'ble Apex Court, vide its judgement dates 13.06.2018, was implemented to address the loss of time faced by the candidates of NEET (UG) 2024.
The loss of examination time was ascertained and such candidates were compensated with grace marks.
So, candidate's marks can be 718 or 719  also"

🚨 NTA awarded grace marks per court order, but students argue this sudden decision is unjust as the agency has not mentioned any methodology to award these ‘grace marks’. Calls for transparency in the process have only grown louder. 

🔍 It gets a little more tricky if we closely notice the roll numbers of students who appeared for the examination from Haryana…

👉 Out of the 8 roll numbers with starting sequence of ‘2307010’ have been reported to belong to the same exam center in the state and have secured top ranks. These unusual patterns in top scorers' roll numbers have further fuelled doubts. Students demand re-evaluation and clear answers.

title: Follow these steps to get 5M views on your next YouTube short…
description:
Follow these steps to get 5M views on your next YouTube short…

Caught in those clickbait headlines again!

Well, the truth is, you can never predict the virality of the content you post.
Having worked on YouTube for many years, I still can't predict the number of views I'll get on my next post.

There have been instances where the content my team and I researched for a month, shot, expecting it to crack more than regular views later sat at average viewership.

On the other hand, another simple idea performed exceptionally well.

I agree with the fact that data and insights offer some trend hints, but there's no guarantee.

No youtube shorts or reels can teach you to go viral in ‘60 secs’.

There's no rulebook for making content. Every creator is different. What works for me can be a flop for you.

Avoid wasting your time searching for YouTube videos on “how to go viral in 5 days”!

Instead, start creating content. Don't wait for the perfect time.

As Stephen Hawking aptly said,

"It is all right to make mistakes; nothing is perfect because with perfection, we would not exist."

title: Ever had your heart race so fast, you could hear it in your ears?
description:
Ever had your heart race so fast, you could hear it in your ears?

In my school days, I had this experience.

It all happened on the stage of a debate competition.

See, I was always the kid who asked tons of questions about everything, from fish breathing underwater (this was just the beginning, trust me) to the mysteries of the universe.  

Knowing my skills and curiosity, my dad got me enrolled me in a debate competition.

I had planned a ton of things to say during the debate. My mind was filled with different opinions, I was fully prepared for my first debate. Rare, right? 

But as soon as the debate started, everyone was firing away their points. I tried to find a pause in the conversation to jump in, but there weren’t any. 

At the end, I spoke nothing, my confidence was shattered. 

Came back and told my Dad that I am going to withdraw my name. 

He heard me, remained calm and said ‘kal ek last try kar, if mann nahi laga toh chod denge’, to which I agreed. 

He then gave me one piece of advice, the advice was simple: when the debate starts, just boldly say, "I don't agree!" Just say it out loud! 

I did the same. That negative statement gave me a chance to speak up and I did. My confidence skyrocketed! 

Suddenly, I was THE man in the debate. 

This experience instilled in me the confidence to address crowds. 

So, If you lack confidence, instead of agreeing on everything, try questioning, try putting your point forward and give it a shot, everything will eventually fall into place.

Did you have such a moment? 

#confidencebuilding #publicspeaking

description:

I felt something similar on my recent trip to London.

I'd been in London for over a week and was really missing Indian food. So, I found an Indian restaurant called "Gymkhana" using Google Maps.

The lady said, "Thank you for your work, beta," and blessed me with all her heart. They were so excited to tell me that they were among my first 50k followers!

It was really different from the usual interaction I have with people, and it felt special.
They told me they'd been living in London for over 30 years but still loved to keep up with what was happening in India.

They used to read newspapers, but now they watch videos and listen to audio content.

Sometimes you don't realize how much of a difference you can make in the world just by doing what you love. Meeting that couple was one of the best experiences I've ever had, and it made me feel amazing.

Whenever I feel down, I think about that moment, and it always cheers me up

title: After joining the corporate world as a fresher and getting promoted to Vice Pres
description:
After joining the corporate world as a fresher and getting promoted to Vice President, I quit my job.

I had gotten into the IT industry straight after college. After 10 years in the industry, I had:

- Worked in multiple leadership roles
- Received various awards and accolades
- Been promoted to my dream position of VP

I had been building this life for over a decade. But I realised I still wasn’t satisfied. I had achieved my goals, but was left wanting more.

I’d always been interested in video editing and content creation. So I decided to dive deeper into this passion, and started a YouTube channel.

There was a lot of figuring out to do — research, scripts, lighting, editing… but I worked long hours after work and made sure I did the best job possible.

Luckily, my effort paid off. My first video was able to impact 500k+ people, and the next few were able to educate millions more.

I saw potential here, but didn’t want to rely on content as my income.

I had also always wanted to build something of my own, so I left my job and stepped into the entrepreneurial landscape, starting an IT consulting company.

A lot of people told me I was making a mistake since my life was ‘sorted’, but I knew I had to follow my heart.

It’s been 3 years since that day, and I’m glad I took that leap.

I live life on my own terms now — running my own company and following my passion of creating videos on topics that matter.

I hope my story proves to you that getting into a particular career doesn’t have to define your entire life.

That’s just the starting point that you chose as a teenager, and you always have the power to change your life’s trajectory.

Keep your eyes open for opportunities, and if one truly appeals to your heart, don’t let it go.

Have you ever pivoted in your career?

#growthmindset #careerdevelopment #entrepreneurship

title: I had to fire one of my talented team members for something that wasn’t his faul
description:
I had to fire one of my talented team members for something that wasn’t his fault.

A few months ago, I had hired Arun (name changed) as a Manager in my company.

His resume was great, he was well-spoken, and seemed quite intelligent. So I was looking forward to having him join us.

But 3 weeks in, some cracks began to appear in this decision.

Arun was a focused worker, but he was also a perfectionist who had difficulties with tight deadlines.

I had no issues with the quality of his work, but he just couldn’t keep up with the fast-paced, high pressure environment at our company.

So after a few months of back-and-forth, I realised he wasn’t the right fit and action was required.

However, I didn’t fire him right off the bat. 

I met him for a 1-on-1 conversation and heard his perspective as well. Together, we came to the conclusion that though he was dedicated to the work, this job just didn’t suit him.

He was quite distraught that we were letting him go, and I didn’t want someone with his skills to struggle for a job either.

So I spoke to a few friends of mine, and got him placed in a research-based job, with lower pressure and less harsh deadlines.

Arun was glad, and he thrived in this environment! He’s still there to this day, and my friend (his boss) speaks highly of him.

So the next time you’re ‘bad at something’, remember that your performance is the result of many internal and external factors.

It’s not necessarily your fault, so figure out what’s affecting you negatively, and try finding an environment you’ll thrive in.

Have you ever been in a similar situation?

title: As a teenager, I used to believe everything I saw on the news, and argued with p
description:
As a teenager, I used to believe everything I saw on the news, and argued with people who disagreed with me.

But as I got older, I realised that I was letting media outlets influence me too easily. 

I was forming opinions too quickly and defending them blindly, without trying to understand the bigger picture.

So I could never stand my ground in arguments, and came off looking ignorant.

As I grew older, I realised I shouldn’t rely upon only one source of information to form an opinion about world events. Because no matter how much a publication claims to be ‘neutral’, it doesn’t tell you the full story.

The writer or media house usually focuses on one side of the events, and it’s only human to have preferences, so that’s not a bad thing.

But I wanted to be fully educated about the topics I spoke about, and found a better way.

I started to:

- Identify relevant experts from both sides
- Read up about their opinions independently
- Form an opinion based on what I felt was right

For example, whenever there is a political dispute in India, I make sure to listen to the perspectives of right-wing and left-wing leaders both, before deciding who I think is being more rational.

I highly suggest you do the same, as this will keep you fully informed, and help you understand the depths of the topic.

Plus if you ever end up discussing it with friends and family, they’ll respect your knowledge even if they have an opposing opinion.

title: I’ve noticed one common mistake that stops aspiring creators from growing their
description:
I’ve noticed one common mistake that stops aspiring creators from growing their channel beyond 100k followers:

We start relying on our content’s monetisation to support us financially.

I’ve realised that if you seriously want to grow your audience, your content should NEVER be your primary source of income. 

If you get too reliant on this, your content will be driven mainly by views. You’ll put yourself under pressure to produce mass-appealing content at a rate where your quality will be compromised.

And if your posts don’t go viral, you’ll be left dejected (and broke).

So if you want to become a serious creator, here are some ways you can safely diversify your monetisation: 

1. Create online courses to share in-depth knowledge. 

2. Collaborate with brands that you truly resonate with.

3. Use affiliate marketing to share products you swear by.

4. Create merch for your fans if you’re passionate about fashion.

But the best option of all:

Create a business and use your online reach as a sales funnel.

I’ve created a community of 4 million+ members, and content creation is still my passion (not my job). So the income from it is just a bonus.

This helps me focus on quality without worrying too much about the results.

title: After interviewing over 150 people throughout my career, I’ve realised that peop
description:
After interviewing over 150 people throughout my career, I’ve realised that people don’t get hired for their CV.

Your resume is just to get your foot in the door — the first round of qualification. 

After that, here’s what recruiters really look for:

1. Commitment

We need to figure out if a candidate is actually passionate and serious about this role, and what their future plans are. People with a long-term vision are great assets to their company, and that’s who we try to find.

2. Coachability

If someone has their ways set in stone, it’s difficult for them to adapt to new situations. What I value are sharp individuals who respond positively to new challenges and pick up new concepts with ease.

3. Experience

I don’t just hire the person with the most years of experience. I look for people who have faced relevant challenges and come out on top. This is what shows me that they’ll be the right fit for the job.

4. Understanding

To help them hit the ground running, new team members need to be able to understand information quickly and act upon it smartly. So I look for people who are intelligent and fast learners.

Please note that CVs are still very important to qualify you for the job and make a good first impression. So put a lot of effort into it to help you stand out.

After that, use this insider knowledge to bring out these qualities in your interview, and nail your job application.

description:
When I started creating content, I made a list of factors that made me dislike a video.

Number 1 on the list was — When the creator doesn’t value my time.

So I made my videos as concise and value-rich as possible, making sure I made the most efficient use of my viewer’s attention.

Here’s how you can do this too:

1. Avoid a typical intro and outro

Avoid the small talk at the beginning and jump straight into the video, and don’t waste time asking people to subscribe at the end.

2. Invest time in research

70% of the time it takes to produce a video should go towards research. This makes your content impactful and points stronger.

3. Try to talk faster

It might sound silly, but doing this helps you pack in more value in a shorter amount of time, and helps you keep their attention.

If you respect your viewers, they’ll respect you too.

So make the best use of their time, cut out the fluff, and watch your community grow.

title: I create content on YouTube for millions of subscribers, while running an IT con
description:
I create content on YouTube for millions of subscribers, while running an IT consulting company.

My secret to managing this? These time management frameworks:


1. Autofocusing

If you’re not a fan of rigid schedules, this free-spirited approach will help you reduce stress and raise productivity.

⚬ Don’t keep a time-table and whenever possible, avoid blocking out time slots. This keeps you flexible and motivated.

⚬ Create 3 lists. A “to-do list” for key tasks, a “watch list” for projects you’re supervising, and a “later list” for the stuff you’d like to do.

⚬ Start when and where you feel like it. Let your motivation and excitement act as a compass to guide which important tasks you should tackle first.


2. The Eisenhower Matrix

When you have too much to do and not enough time, prioritisation is key. Write down your tasks with 2 checkboxes next to them - ‘Important’ and ‘Urgent’.

⚬ Important + Urgent = DO

⚬ Important + Not Urgent = DECIDE

⚬ Urgent + Not Important = DELEGATE

⚬ Not Urgent + Not Important = DELETE


3. The Pomodoro Method

Short burst of focused work >>> Hours of sitting at your desk distracted. This technique uses this philosophy to cut out interruptions and battle fatigue.

⚬ Identify a specific task, and sit at your desk without any distractions (put your phone on silent).

⚬ Set a timer for 25 minutes and begin your work. Don’t let anything take your attention away from the task at hand.

⚬ When the timer goes off, take a 5 minute break.

⚬ Break this cycle with a longer, 30 minute pause for every 4th break.

It sounds easy, but it’s so effective!


I live by these 3 frameworks, and I’m glad I put in the time to research these early on in my career.

Try these out, and you’ll get more done than ever in just a day’s work.

It’s simple — If a task takes less than 2 minutes, do it RIGHT NOW without pushing it for the future.

title: *Will AI Take Jobs? Have You Experienced It?*
description:
*Will AI Take Jobs? Have You Experienced It?*

All the buzz these days is about AI, all we hear there says is AI or Artificial Intelligence. Everyone around us talks about AI. Is it worth the hype? Are the claims of AI takeover true?

Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly evolving, and there is growing concern that it will lead to job losses. Some experts believe that AI will automate many jobs, while others believe that it will create new jobs.

So, what is the truth? Will AI take jobs?

The answer is not simple. It is likely that AI will automate some jobs, but it is also likely that it will create new jobs. The net effect of AI on jobs is still uncertain.

However, there are some trends that we can already see. For example, AI is already being used to automate tasks in manufacturing, customer service, and healthcare. This has led to job losses in some of these industries.

At the same time, AI is also creating new jobs. For example, there is a growing demand for AI engineers and data scientists. These are the people who are responsible for developing and deploying AI systems.

So, what does this mean for you? If you are worried about AI taking your job, there are a few things you can do. First, you can start learning about AI and how it is being used in your industry. This will help you to understand the potential impact of AI on your job.

Second, you can start developing skills that are complementary to AI. For example, if you are a customer service representative, you could start learning about AI customer service chatbots. This will help you to stay relevant in your job even as AI automates some of your tasks.

Finally, you can be proactive about your career. Don't wait for AI to take your job. Start looking for new opportunities that will allow you to leverage your skills and experience in the age of AI.

title: The Changing Landscape of Work
description:
The Changing Landscape of Work

Over the years, there has been a significant shift in the way we approach work, I have noticed and implemented it myself. So today I want to discuss with you all of what you think about this change in the industry?

In the past, a college degree was everything and people were obsessed with having one.

However, with the changing times, the industry is now shifting towards a more skill-based hiring process and major companies have even begun removing the college degree requirement for certain positions.

Employers now value skills obtained through alternative routes such as online courses, vocational training, and apprenticeships, creating a more inclusive workforce.

Another advantage of skill-based hiring is that it allows employers to focus on what really matters - the skills required for the job.

This approach to hiring ensures that the right candidate is selected for the job based on their skills and not just their academic qualifications. It also helps in closing the skills gap that exists in the job market, as employers are now able to identify candidates with the specific skills required for the job.

In my opinion, it is a welcome change but I’m more interested to know your views on this, let me know your take on this new direction the industry is heading to, in the comments below.

- Arab people who settled there before 1925.
- Children born to existing UAE nationals.

Getting a citizenship through marriage isn’t easy either.

- In 7 years if they have a child together.

description:
#Research

My YouTube channel recently hit 2.5 million subscribers, and there’s one key factor I attribute this growth to:

My research process.

This allows me to create highly relevant, unbiased and fact-driven content that helped me reach huge audiences.

The best part? It all happens on 3 Google tools, which are completely free to use.

Today, I’m sharing this process with you.

1. Create a framework

Search for books on the topic you’ve chosen. You can then preview these on Google Books, and see the index. Use this to create a structure for your content piece.

2. Find resources

Google Scholar is a researcher’s best friend. Find relevant published articles, use Ctrl+F to look for specific points, and compile these on a document.

3. Dig deeper

Let’s say you’re researching AI tools. Use Google Advanced Search to narrow search results, using these commands:

- related:chatgpt - Helps you find pages related to a given topic.
- filetype:pdf - Use this to find reports and analyses.
- after:2022 - Get more recent, relevant results.

Change the keywords after the : based on your topic.

Once you have all this refined information within your reach, all you have to do is write your script and move towards the production.

Which of these tools will you be incorporating into your research process?

title: 🚨 An Indian vessel has reportedly sunk in the Red Sea. Thankfully, all 13 Indian sailors were rescued. But the bigger question remains: Who was behind
description:
🚨 An Indian vessel has reportedly sunk in the Red Sea. Thankfully, all 13 Indian sailors were rescued. But the bigger question remains: Who was behind the attack?

On 4 August 2026, the Indian vessel MSV Faize Noore Oliya reportedly sank near Yemen after being struck by what is believed to have been a rocket or drone.

According to available reports, the Yemeni Coast Guard successfully rescued all 13 Indian crew members.

However, responsibility for the attack remains officially unconfirmed.
The Yemeni government has accused the Iran-backed Houthi movement, while India's Ministry of External Affairs has described the incident as "deeply concerning" but has not attributed the attack to any specific group.

This incident comes at a time when global shipping routes are already under pressure due to tensions in the Middle East. With disruptions around the Strait of Hormuz, many commercial vessels have increasingly relied on the Red Sea corridor one of the world's most strategically important maritime routes.

If the attack is eventually confirmed to have targeted an Indian vessel, despite India having no direct conflict with the Houthis, it could have significant implications for regional maritime security and India's commercial interests.

As investigations continue, the focus remains on establishing the facts and ensuring the safety of international shipping.

NEET UG-2024 results were declared recently and a record number of 67 students secured AIR 1 with a percentile score of 99.997129. 
But the results have raised eyebrows at the National Testing Agency (NTA) as students demand re-exam citing paper leaks, unfair grace marks, and irregularities.

Here’s what happened…

👉  Right after the results were declared, questions were asked on how such an unprecedented number (67) of students secured 720/720 and AIR 1. The number in 2023 was just 2, with students belonging from Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh.

The loss of examination time was ascertained and such candidates were compensated with grace marks.
So, candidate's marks can be 718 or 719  also"

🚨 NTA awarded grace marks per court order, but students argue this sudden decision is unjust as the agency has not mentioned any methodology to award these ‘grace marks’. Calls for transparency in the process have only grown louder. 

🔍 It gets a little more tricky if we closely notice the roll numbers of students who appeared for the examination from Haryana…

👉 Out of the 8 roll numbers with starting sequence of ‘2307010’ have been reported to belong to the same exam center in the state and have secured top ranks. These unusual patterns in top scorers' roll numbers have further fuelled doubts. Students demand re-evaluation and clear answers.

description:
Follow these steps to get 5M views on your next YouTube short…

Caught in those clickbait headlines again!

Well, the truth is, you can never predict the virality of the content you post.
Having worked on YouTube for many years, I still can't predict the number of views I'll get on my next post.

There have been instances where the content my team and I researched for a month, shot, expecting it to crack more than regular views later sat at average viewership.

On the other hand, another simple idea performed exceptionally well.

I agree with the fact that data and insights offer some trend hints, but there's no guarantee.

No youtube shorts or reels can teach you to go viral in ‘60 secs’.

There's no rulebook for making content. Every creator is different. What works for me can be a flop for you.

Avoid wasting your time searching for YouTube videos on “how to go viral in 5 days”!

Instead, start creating content. Don't wait for the perfect time.

As Stephen Hawking aptly said,

"It is all right to make mistakes; nothing is perfect because with perfection, we would not exist."

Ever had your heart race so fast, you could hear it in your ears?

In my school days, I had this experience.

It all happened on the stage of a debate
description:
Ever had your heart race so fast, you could hear it in your ears?

In my school days, I had this experience.

It all happened on the stage of a debate competition.

See, I was always the kid who asked tons of questions about everything, from fish breathing underwater (this was just the beginning, trust me) to the mysteries of the universe.  

Knowing my skills and curiosity, my dad got me enrolled me in a debate competition.

I had planned a ton of things to say during the debate. My mind was filled with different opinions, I was fully prepared for my first debate. Rare, right? 

But as soon as the debate started, everyone was firing away their points. I tried to find a pause in the conversation to jump in, but there weren’t any. 

At the end, I spoke nothing, my confidence was shattered. 

Came back and told my Dad that I am going to withdraw my name. 

He heard me, remained calm and said ‘kal ek last try kar, if mann nahi laga toh chod denge’, to which I agreed. 

He then gave me one piece of advice, the advice was simple: when the debate starts, just boldly say, "I don't agree!" Just say it out loud! 

I did the same. That negative statement gave me a chance to speak up and I did. My confidence skyrocketed! 

Suddenly, I was THE man in the debate. 

This experience instilled in me the confidence to address crowds. 

So, If you lack confidence, instead of agreeing on everything, try questioning, try putting your point forward and give it a shot, everything will eventually fall into place.

Did you have such a moment? 

#confidencebuilding #publicspeaking

You know that feeling of warmth and pure comfort when you eat your mother's homemade aloo paratha with lots of butter?

They told me they'd been living in London for over 30 years but still loved to keep up with what was happening in India.

They used to read newspapers, but now they watch videos and listen to audio content.

Sometimes you don't realize how much of a difference you can make in the world just by doing what you love. Meeting that couple was one of the best experiences I've ever had, and it made me feel amazing.

description:
After joining the corporate world as a fresher and getting promoted to Vice President, I quit my job.

I had gotten into the IT industry straight after college. After 10 years in the industry, I had:

- Worked in multiple leadership roles
- Received various awards and accolades
- Been promoted to my dream position of VP

I had been building this life for over a decade. But I realised I still wasn’t satisfied. I had achieved my goals, but was left wanting more.

I’d always been interested in video editing and content creation. So I decided to dive deeper into this passion, and started a YouTube channel.

There was a lot of figuring out to do — research, scripts, lighting, editing… but I worked long hours after work and made sure I did the best job possible.

Luckily, my effort paid off. My first video was able to impact 500k+ people, and the next few were able to educate millions more.

I saw potential here, but didn’t want to rely on content as my income.

I had also always wanted to build something of my own, so I left my job and stepped into the entrepreneurial landscape, starting an IT consulting company.

A lot of people told me I was making a mistake since my life was ‘sorted’, but I knew I had to follow my heart.

It’s been 3 years since that day, and I’m glad I took that leap.

I live life on my own terms now — running my own company and following my passion of creating videos on topics that matter.

I hope my story proves to you that getting into a particular career doesn’t have to define your entire life.

That’s just the starting point that you chose as a teenager, and you always have the power to change your life’s trajectory.

Keep your eyes open for opportunities, and if one truly appeals to your heart, don’t let it go.

Have you ever pivoted in your career?

#growthmindset #careerdevelopment #entrepreneurship

description:
I had to fire one of my talented team members for something that wasn’t his fault.

A few months ago, I had hired Arun (name changed) as a Manager in my company.

His resume was great, he was well-spoken, and seemed quite intelligent. So I was looking forward to having him join us.

But 3 weeks in, some cracks began to appear in this decision.

Arun was a focused worker, but he was also a perfectionist who had difficulties with tight deadlines.

I had no issues with the quality of his work, but he just couldn’t keep up with the fast-paced, high pressure environment at our company.

So after a few months of back-and-forth, I realised he wasn’t the right fit and action was required.

However, I didn’t fire him right off the bat. 

I met him for a 1-on-1 conversation and heard his perspective as well. Together, we came to the conclusion that though he was dedicated to the work, this job just didn’t suit him.

He was quite distraught that we were letting him go, and I didn’t want someone with his skills to struggle for a job either.

So I spoke to a few friends of mine, and got him placed in a research-based job, with lower pressure and less harsh deadlines.

Arun was glad, and he thrived in this environment! He’s still there to this day, and my friend (his boss) speaks highly of him.

So the next time you’re ‘bad at something’, remember that your performance is the result of many internal and external factors.

It’s not necessarily your fault, so figure out what’s affecting you negatively, and try finding an environment you’ll thrive in.

Have you ever been in a similar situation?

#workculture #careergrowth #entrepreneurship

description:
As a teenager, I used to believe everything I saw on the news, and argued with people who disagreed with me.

But as I got older, I realised that I was letting media outlets influence me too easily. 

I was forming opinions too quickly and defending them blindly, without trying to understand the bigger picture.

So I could never stand my ground in arguments, and came off looking ignorant.

As I grew older, I realised I shouldn’t rely upon only one source of information to form an opinion about world events. Because no matter how much a publication claims to be ‘neutral’, it doesn’t tell you the full story.

The writer or media house usually focuses on one side of the events, and it’s only human to have preferences, so that’s not a bad thing.

But I wanted to be fully educated about the topics I spoke about, and found a better way.

I started to:

- Identify relevant experts from both sides
- Read up about their opinions independently
- Form an opinion based on what I felt was right

For example, whenever there is a political dispute in India, I make sure to listen to the perspectives of right-wing and left-wing leaders both, before deciding who I think is being more rational.

I highly suggest you do the same, as this will keep you fully informed, and help you understand the depths of the topic.

Plus if you ever end up discussing it with friends and family, they’ll respect your knowledge even if they have an opposing opinion.

description:
I’ve noticed one common mistake that stops aspiring creators from growing their channel beyond 100k followers:

We start relying on our content’s monetisation to support us financially.

I’ve realised that if you seriously want to grow your audience, your content should NEVER be your primary source of income. 

If you get too reliant on this, your content will be driven mainly by views. You’ll put yourself under pressure to produce mass-appealing content at a rate where your quality will be compromised.

And if your posts don’t go viral, you’ll be left dejected (and broke).

So if you want to become a serious creator, here are some ways you can safely diversify your monetisation: 

1. Create online courses to share in-depth knowledge. 

2. Collaborate with brands that you truly resonate with.

3. Use affiliate marketing to share products you swear by.

4. Create merch for your fans if you’re passionate about fashion.

But the best option of all:

Create a business and use your online reach as a sales funnel.

I’ve created a community of 4 million+ members, and content creation is still my passion (not my job). So the income from it is just a bonus.

This helps me focus on quality without worrying too much about the results.

description:
After interviewing over 150 people throughout my career, I’ve realised that people don’t get hired for their CV.

Your resume is just to get your foot in the door — the first round of qualification. 

After that, here’s what recruiters really look for:

1. Commitment

We need to figure out if a candidate is actually passionate and serious about this role, and what their future plans are. People with a long-term vision are great assets to their company, and that’s who we try to find.

2. Coachability

If someone has their ways set in stone, it’s difficult for them to adapt to new situations. What I value are sharp individuals who respond positively to new challenges and pick up new concepts with ease.

3. Experience

I create content on YouTube for millions of subscribers, while running an IT consulting company.

My secret to managing this? These time management frameworks:


1. Autofocusing

If you’re not a fan of rigid schedules, this free-spirited approach will help you reduce stress and raise productivity.

⚬ Don’t keep a time-table and whenever possible, avoid blocking out time slots. This keeps you flexible and motivated.

⚬ Create 3 lists. A “to-do list” for key tasks, a “watch list” for projects you’re supervising, and a “later list” for the stuff you’d like to do.

⚬ Start when and where you feel like it. Let your motivation and excitement act as a compass to guide which important tasks you should tackle first.


2. The Eisenhower Matrix

When you have too much to do and not enough time, prioritisation is key. Write down your tasks with 2 checkboxes next to them - ‘Important’ and ‘Urgent’.

⚬ Important + Urgent = DO

⚬ Important + Not Urgent = DECIDE

⚬ Urgent + Not Important = DELEGATE

⚬ Not Urgent + Not Important = DELETE


3. The Pomodoro Method

Short burst of focused work >>> Hours of sitting at your desk distracted. This technique uses this philosophy to cut out interruptions and battle fatigue.

⚬ Identify a specific task, and sit at your desk without any distractions (put your phone on silent).

⚬ Set a timer for 25 minutes and begin your work. Don’t let anything take your attention away from the task at hand.

⚬ When the timer goes off, take a 5 minute break.

⚬ Break this cycle with a longer, 30 minute pause for every 4th break.

It sounds easy, but it’s so effective!


I live by these 3 frameworks, and I’m glad I put in the time to research these early on in my career.

Try these out, and you’ll get more done than ever in just a day’s work.

*Will AI Take Jobs? Have You Experienced It?*

All the buzz these days is about AI, all we hear there says is AI or Artificial Intelligence. Everyone around us talks about AI. Is it worth the hype? Are the claims of AI takeover true?

Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly evolving, and there is growing concern that it will lead to job losses. Some experts believe that AI will automate many jobs, while others believe that it will create new jobs.

So, what is the truth? Will AI take jobs?

The answer is not simple. It is likely that AI will automate some jobs, but it is also likely that it will create new jobs. The net effect of AI on jobs is still uncertain.

However, there are some trends that we can already see. For example, AI is already being used to automate tasks in manufacturing, customer service, and healthcare. This has led to job losses in some of these industries.

At the same time, AI is also creating new jobs. For example, there is a growing demand for AI engineers and data scientists. These are the people who are responsible for developing and deploying AI systems.

So, what does this mean for you? If you are worried about AI taking your job, there are a few things you can do. First, you can start learning about AI and how it is being used in your industry. This will help you to understand the potential impact of AI on your job.

Second, you can start developing skills that are complementary to AI. For example, if you are a customer service representative, you could start learning about AI customer service chatbots. This will help you to stay relevant in your job even as AI automates some of your tasks.

Over the years, there has been a significant shift in the way we approach work, I have noticed and implemented it myself. So today I want to discuss with you all of what you think about this change in the industry?

In the past, a college degree was everything and people were obsessed with having one.

However, with the changing times, the industry is now shifting towards a more skill-based hiring process and major companies have even begun removing the college degree requirement for certain positions.

Employers now value skills obtained through alternative routes such as online courses, vocational training, and apprenticeships, creating a more inclusive workforce.

This approach to hiring ensures that the right candidate is selected for the job based on their skills and not just their academic qualifications. It also helps in closing the skills gap that exists in the job market, as employers are now able to identify candidates with the specific skills required for the job.

My YouTube channel recently hit 2.5 million subscribers, and there’s one key factor I attribute this growth to:

My research process.

This allows me to create highly relevant, unbiased and fact-driven content that helped me reach huge audiences.

The best part? It all happens on 3 Google tools, which are completely free to use.

Today, I’m sharing this process with you.

1. Create a framework

Search for books on the topic you’ve chosen. You can then preview these on Google Books, and see the index. Use this to create a structure for your content piece.

2. Find resources

Google Scholar is a researcher’s best friend. Find relevant published articles, use Ctrl+F to look for specific points, and compile these on a document.

3. Dig deeper

Let’s say you’re researching AI tools. Use Google Advanced Search to narrow search results, using these commands:

- related:chatgpt - Helps you find pages related to a given topic.
- filetype:pdf - Use this to find reports and analyses.
- after:2022 - Get more recent, relevant results.

Change the keywords after the : based on your topic.

Once you have all this refined information within your reach, all you have to do is write your script and move towards the production.
